Ms. Adams. Thank you, Mr. Chairman, and thank you to our 
witnesses. Today's hearing could have been an opportunity to 
work together to tackle the real challenges facing students and 
families. Instead we have seen a partisan attempt to 
manufacture outrage over a respected scholarship program while 
ignoring the growing crisis of college affordability and 
student debt.
    Let us not lose sight of what is at stake. The average cost 
of college has skyrocketed. Tens of millions of Americans are 
carrying student debt that impacts every aspect of their lives, 
from starting a family, to saving for retirement. This burden 
falls heaviest on those already facing systemic inequality, 
women, first generation students, and communities of color.
    Instead of offering solutions, Republicans passed the Big 
Ugly Law, a policy that slashes financial aid, eliminates key 
protections and increases monthly payments for most borrowers, 
all while the Trump administration is illegally dismantling the 
Department of Education, including the Office of Postsecondary 
Education.
    Together, these actions by Republicans make it harder to go 
to college, harder to stay in college, and harder to recover 
financially after graduation. Democrats are offering a better 
way forward. The Lowering Obstacles to Achievement Now, LOAN, 
this act would double Pell Grants, would lower interest rates, 
and ensure student loan repayment is fair, and manageable.
    It is a real plan to fix a real problem. The American 
people do not want political theater. They want us to lower 
costs, expand opportunity, and give every student a fair shot, 
and that is what we are fighting for. Thank you again to all of 
our witnesses and Mr. Chairman, I yield back.
